title: Platform systems & services playbook: dashboards, alerts, runbooks, roadmap, team wiki (v2)
author: Daniel Kim
content:
Overview

This document is the canonical platform engineering playbook for systems & services: a centralized reference for the team wiki covering system owners, SLOs, dashboards, alerting, runbooks, retrospectives, and the near-term roadmap. Intended audience: platform engineers, on-call SREs, infra engineers, and engineering managers.

Quick links
- Grafana: https://grafana.internal.redwood/team/platform
- Alertmanager: https://alertmanager.internal.redwood
- PagerDuty: https://pagerduty.com/teams/redwood-platform
- Metrics docs: /confluence/eng-platform/metrics-and-telemetry

1) Systems & services inventory (high level)

The following table summarizes the primary platform services, owners, and SLOs. Services not listed are either product-facing and owned by product teams or deprecated.

| Service | Owner | Primary purpose | SLO (availability / latency) | Dashboard |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| platform-api | platform-api team (oncall: platform-api) | Internal control plane APIs (deploy, config, quota) | 99.95% p99 < 200ms | grafana/dashboard/db/platform-api-overview |
| metrics-ingestor | telemetry team | Ingest, validate, and forward telemetry (OTLP -> Kafka) | 99.9% ingest success; median processing < 1s | grafana/dashboard/db/metrics-ingestor |
| metrics-store (Cortex) | observability team | Long-term metrics, query layer | 99.9% query availability; p95 query < 350ms | grafana/dashboard/db/cortex-queries |
| auth-gateway | platform-security | RBAC/token validation for internal services | 99.99% availability | grafana/dashboard/db/auth-gateway |
| k8s-clusters (platform) | infra-k8s | Multi-cluster control plane for platform workloads | Control-plane SLO: 99.9% API availability | grafana/dashboard/db/k8s-controlplane |
| ingress/router | infra-network | Edge routing for internal and external traffic | 99.95% request success; p99 < 120ms | grafana/dashboard/db/ingress-router |

2) Dashboards & alerting matrix

Design principles
- Dashboards are organized by persona: On-call, Engineering, Product/Capacity. Default landing page is the On-call overview.
- Alerts must be actionable, paged only when human intervention is required. Use severity labels: SEV-1 (pager, phone), SEV-2 (pager), SEV-3 (email/Slack).
- Keep MTTD low by surfacing the most likely root causes (downstream, OOM, throttling, excessive 5xxs).

Key dashboards to maintain
- On-call overview (high-level health across platform stacks).
- Platform-api: latency, error-rate, top 5 endpoints, dependency latencies (auth, metrics-store).
- Metrics pipeline: Kafka lag, OTLP drop rate, processing latency.
- Cortex / metrics-store: series churn, compaction backlog, query latency.

Alert catalog (examples)
- ALERT: platform_api_high_5xx_rate (SEV-2)
  - Trigger: sustained >1% 5xx rate on platform-api for 5m and >50 rps
  - Pager duty: platform-api oncall
  - Runbook: section 'Runbook: Platform API high error rate' below
- ALERT: metrics_ingestor_kafka_lag_high (SEV-2)
  - Trigger: consumer lag > 1M messages for 10m
  - Pager duty: telemetry oncall
  - Runbook: section 'Runbook: Metrics ingestion pipeline lag'
- ALERT: cortex_query_error_rate (SEV-2)
  - Trigger: query error rate >0.5% for 5m or p95 latency > 1s
  - Pager duty: observability oncall

3) Standard runbooks (headlines + step-by-step)

Runbook: Platform API — high error rate (platform_api_high_5xx_rate)
1) Triage
   - Check On-call overview dashboard and platform-api dashboard. Confirm scope: single region, single instance group, or global.
   - Identify recent deploys (check CI/CD pipeline / deploy timeline).
2) Mitigation (if impacting customers / internal tooling)
   - If deploy is suspected: roll back the last canary or canary traffic to 0% (CI/CD -> Rollback button).
   - If resource exhaustion on pods: scale deployment replicas to +50% and redeploy (kubectl rollout restart).
   - If requests are being throttled by auth-gateway: temporarily disable strict rate limiter for platform-api (feature flag: rate-limit:platform-api -> set to permissive).
3) Root cause & remediation
   - Capture logs (kubectl logs -n platform deployment/platform-api --since=15m) and trace spans (Jaeger traces: filter by trace tag service=platform-api).
   - Open a postmortem if SEV-1 or recurring SEV-2 happened in last 90 days. Assign RCA owner.

Runbook: Metrics ingestion pipeline lag (metrics_ingestor_kafka_lag_high)
1) Triage
   - Check Kafka consumer lag (grafana) and broker health. Confirm retention settings and disk pressure.
2) Mitigation
   - If consumer backpressure due to CPU/memory: increase consumer replicas or CPU limit.
   - If broker IO pressure: follow infra runbook to provision ephemeral storage or throttle producers.
3) Follow-up
   - Add defensive rate limits or consent to drop non-critical telemetry. Create dashboard for producer-side error spikes.

Runbook: Missing metrics / Alert noise (metrics_missing)
1) Verify agent health (otel-collector pods, node-exporter).
2) Restart collector(s) if necessary and check local disk usage.
3) If missing persists, escalate to telemetry team.

4) How-tos (short how-to procedures)

How to add a new Grafana dashboard
1) Create dashboard in grafana using dashboard templating for cluster/region variables.
2) Add required panels: health summary, latency, errors, top callers. Keep panels <= 12 to remain readable.
3) Add panel descriptions and runbook links (link to this doc).
4) Save as team: "Platform" and submit PR to /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards for review.

How to tune an alert threshold
1) Check historical metric (30d) to understand baseline and seasonal patterns.
2) Simulate alert conditions in staging if possible (load test).
3) Update rule with an appropriate evaluation window and silence interval. Document the change in the alert rule change log.

How to create an SLO and wire it to alerting
1) Define the consumer-visible objective and measurement window (30d rolling recommended).
2) Implement the SLI using a robust numerator/denominator (e.g., successful API responses / total successful+failed).
3) Create grafana panel + scoreboard. Create alert for burn rate > 2x target for 1h (SEV-2).
4) Review with product owners and sign off.

5) Retrospective: summary of notable incidents (Q3 — Q4 2026)

Summary (Q3 2026)
- Incident: Metrics ingestion lag spike (2026-08-11) — root cause: Kafka broker IO saturation due to untriaged retention misconfig after a perf test.
  - Impact: delayed metrics for 3 hours, alert noise.
  - Action items: implement pre-test capacity checklist, increase Kafka broker IO alerting sensitivity, add canary metrics producer.

Summary (Q4 2026)
- Incident: Platform API increased 5xx rate after a library upgrade (2026-11-03) — root cause: incompatible client updates causing malformed requests.
  - Impact: internal CI/CD and customer provisioning failures for 45 minutes.
  - Action items: add integration test that validates client/server contract, tighten canary rollout threshold to 5% for 30m, and add automatic rollback on 5xx >0.5% for 10m.

Action item tracker (status)
- Pre-test capacity checklist: assigned to infra-k8s, due 2026-02-28 (status: done).
- Contract integration tests: assigned to platform-api team, due 2027-01-15 (status: in_progress).
- Alert noise review: observability team, due 2026-12-15 (status: completed).

6) Roadmap (next 6–12 months)
- Q1 2027: Migrate metrics pipeline to OTLP-first architecture and standardize tracing headers across services.
- Q2 2027: Migrate alerting to Cortex Alertmanager federation and introduce auto-snooze for known maintenance windows.
- Q2 2027: Implement adaptive autoscaling for platform workloads based on request qps and queue length (pilot on ingress/router).
- Q3 2027: Unified cost & capacity dashboards for Dedicated and Private offerings; per-customer capacity tagging.
- Ongoing: Runbook automation framework (playbooks-as-code) + richer PagerDuty automation for common remediations.

7) Team wiki & onboarding checklist
- Required reading for new platform hires: this playbook, metrics-and-telemetry, k8s-clusters-runbooks, infra-networking-basics.
- Onboarding tasks (first 30 days): set up Grafana + PagerDuty access, complete local dev cluster setup, shadow oncall twice, contribute a dashboard fix.

8) Ownership, escalation matrix, and contact list
| Role | Name | PagerDuty | Slack |
|---|---|---|---|
| Platform lead | Daniel Kim | N/A | #team-platform |
| Platform-api oncall | rotation: platform-api | platform-api@pagerduty.com | @platform-api-oncall |
| Observability oncall | rotation: observability | observability@pagerduty.com | @observability-oncall |
| Telemetry oncall | rotation: telemetry | telemetry@pagerduty.com | @telemetry-oncall |

Escalation rules
- SEV-1: page primary oncall then escalate to secondary after 10m, then platform lead after 20m.
- SEV-2: page primary oncall, message #platform-ops Slack channel.

Appendix: diagnostics commands and snippets
- kubectl logs -n platform deployment/platform-api --since=15m | grep ERROR
- kafka-topics --describe --zookeeper zk1:2181 --topic telemetry-topic
- promql examples: rate(platform_api_request_duration_seconds_count[5m]) / rate(platform_api_request_duration_seconds_sum[5m])
